#**Overview**


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment=NA, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(psych)
library(knitr)
library(tidyr)
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(gridExtra)
library(Rmisc)
library(lsr)
```


This document presents the data analysis for the reddit study.

#Data Cleaning

```{r}
d_RAW <- read.csv("Reddit_Survey_72519_new_url.csv")

d_RAWish <- d_RAW %>%
  dplyr::filter(condition != "") %>%
  dplyr::filter(condition != "condition") %>%
  dplyr::filter(V10 == 1)

d_full <- d_RAWish %>%
  dplyr::select(condition, other_party, other_attitude, starts_with("Q"), starts_with("dem"), starts_with("optin"), FR.question)

write.csv(d_full, "full dataset.csv")
d_full <- read.csv("full dataset.csv")

d <- d_full %>%
  dplyr::filter(Q9.compcheck == 1)

write.csv(d, "clean data - to code.csv", row.names=FALSE)
d <- read.csv("clean data - coded.csv")

d <- filter(d, Exclude != "Y")

write.csv(d, "Reddit data with exclusions removed.csv")
```


We begin with the full dataset of 568 people who completed the survey, then remove everyone who failed the attention check, or who did not follow directions (by not writing an argument, or writing an argument for the wrong side)

Consistent with our preregistration plan, we excluded 84 (14.8%) who failed the attention check or did not follow instructions, leaving a sample of 484 participants (44.4% female, Mage = 30.57).


#Descriptive Statistics

##Participant gender

1 indicates female, 2 indicates male, 3 indicates other, 4 indicates prefer not to answer

```{r}
table(d$dem.gender)
```

##Participant Age

Mean and CI age:
```{r}
CI(filter(d, is.na(dem.age) == FALSE)$dem.age, ci=0.95)
mean(d$dem.age, na.rm=TRUE)
```

\newpage

#Initial Attitude

We begin by comparing the initial distribution of attitudes by condition, to confirm random assignment.
```{r}
d_PT <- filter(d, condition == "PT")
d_control <- filter(d, condition == "control")
t.test(d_PT$Q1.attT1_1, d_control$Q1.attT1_1)
```

Control:
```{r}
CI(d_control$Q1.attT1_1)
```

Perspective Taking:
```{r}
CI(d_PT$Q1.attT1_1)
```

Initial attitudes did not differ between the control (M = 81.48, 95% CI [77.93, 85.03]) and perspective-taking (M = 81.61, 95% CI [77.82, 85.38]) conditions, t(482) = 0.05, p = .96.


#Midpoint

How many people indicated the midpoint?
```{r}
d_50 <- filter(d, Q1.attT1_1 == 50)
nrow(d_50)

d_noneutral <- filter(d, Q1.attT1_1 != 50)
```

Participants who indicated a neutral attitude (exactly the midpoint; N = 2) were randomly assigned to a side; removing these participants doesn't affect significance tests.


\newpage

#Receptiveness

Receptiveness is measured by 4 items, specifically:

- How receptive do you feel toward the specific argument that you wrote about?

- How open-minded do you feel toward the specific argument that you wrote about? 

- How receptive do you feel toward the perspective (in favor of /against UBI) in general?

- How open-minded do you feel toward the perspective (in favor of/against UBI) in general?

##Creating an index for receptiveness

We begin by computing the alpha for receptiveness:

```{r}
receptiveness <- dplyr::select(d, Q3.receparg, Q4.recepoarg, Q5.recepgen, Q6.recepogen)
alphaRecep <- psych::alpha(receptiveness)
kable(alphaRecep$total)
```

Because our alpha is acceptable (alpha = 0.85), we then combine the 4 receptiveness items into a single index.
```{r}
d$receptiveness <- (d$Q3.receparg + d$Q4.recepoarg + d$Q5.recepgen + d$Q6.recepogen)/4
```


\newpage

#Effect of condition on receptiveness

To explore the effect of condition on receptiveness, we employ an unpaired samples t-test, assuming approximately equal variances 

```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
perspective <- filter(d, condition == "PT")
control <- filter(d, condition == "control")
t.test(perspective$receptiveness, control$receptiveness, paired=FALSE, var.equal=TRUE)
```

Cohen's D:
```{r}
cohensD(perspective$receptiveness, control$receptiveness)
```

Control:
```{r}
CI(control$receptiveness, ci = 0.95)
```
Perspective Taking:
```{r}
CI(perspective$receptiveness, ci = 0.95)
```

Participants reported less receptiveness to the counterattitudinal view in the perspective-taking (M = 3.27, 95% CI [3.11, 3.43]) relative to control (M = 3.53, 95% CI [3.36, 3.69]) condition, t(482)=-2.15, p = .032. 

 

#Graph

```{r}
se_plus <- function(x) mean(x) + sqrt(var(x)/length(x))
se_minus <- function(x) mean(x) - sqrt(var(x)/length(x))

limits <- aes(ymax = se_u, ymin= se_l)
dodge <- position_dodge(width=0.9)

summary <- d %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(condition) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise("Receptiveness" = mean(receptiveness, na.rm=TRUE), "se_u"=se_plus(receptiveness), "se_l"=se_minus(receptiveness)) 

p1 <- ggplot(data=summary, aes(x=condition, y=Receptiveness, fill=condition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") + 
  geom_errorbar(limits, position=dodge, width=0.25) + 
  labs(x="Condition", y="Receptiveness") +
  guides(fill=FALSE) +
  theme_hc() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(2, 4))


p1
```

\newpage

#Attitude Change

We calculate attitude change toward the counterattitudinal position for all participants, such that positive numbers always indicate movement in the counterattitudinal direction, while negative numbers indicate movement in the proattitudinal direction.

```{r}
d$att.change <- ifelse(d$other_attitude == "in support of", d$Q2.att_1 - d$Q1.attT1_1, NA)

d$att.change <- ifelse(d$other_attitude == "against", d$Q1.attT1_1 - d$Q2.att_1, d$att.change)
```

#Effect of Condition on Attitude Change

```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
perspective <- filter(d, condition == "PT")
control <- filter(d, condition == "control")
t.test(perspective$att.change,
       control$att.change,
       paired=FALSE, var.equal=TRUE)
```

Cohen's D:
```{r}
cohensD(perspective$att.change, control$att.change)
```

Control:
```{r}
CI(control$att.change, ci=0.95)
```
Perspective Taking:
```{r}
CI(perspective$att.change, ci=0.95)
```

Participants showed less change toward the counterattitudinal view in the perspective-taking (M = 0.39, 95% CI [-0.17, 0.94]) relative to control (M = 1.52, 95% CI [0.55, 2.50]) condition, t(482)=-1.98, p = 0.048.


\newpage

se_minus <- function(x) mean(x) - sqrt(var(x)/length(x))

#Value/Moral Congruence

Value/Moral Congruence is measured by 3 items, specifically:

- To what extent is this argument congruent with your own values?

- To what extent does this argument fit with your worldview?

- To what extent does this argument reflect your own personal morals?

## Creating an index for value congruence

We begin by computing the alpha for value congruence

```{r, echo=FALSE}
valuecongruence <- dplyr::select(d, Q7.valueco, Q7.valuewv, Q8.valuemoral)
alphaCongruence <- psych::alpha(valuecongruence)
kable(alphaCongruence$total)
```

Because alpha is satisfactory (alpha = 0.88), we create a single index for value congruence. I've also recoded it so that higher means more congruent. 

```{r}
d$congruence <- 8 - (d$Q7.valueco + d$Q7.valuewv + d$Q8.valuemoral)/3
```

\newpage

##Effect of condition on value congruence

To explore the effect of condition on receptiveness, we employ anunpaired samples t-test, assuming approximately equal variances


```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
perspective <- filter(d, condition == "PT")
control <- filter(d, condition == "control")
t.test(perspective$congruence,
       control$congruence,
       paired=FALSE, var.equal=TRUE)
```

Cohen's D:
```{r}
cohensD(perspective$congruence, control$congruence)
```

Perspective:
```{r}
CI(perspective$congruence, ci=.95)
```
Control:
```{r}
CI(control$congruence, ci = .95)
```

Participants reported less value-congruent arguments in the perspective-taking (M = 2.91, 95% CI [2.71, 3.11]) relative to control (M = 3.25, 95% CI [3.04, 3.46]) condition, t(482)=-2.30, p = .02. 


\newpage

# Mediation 1: Condition -> Congruence -> Receptiveness

In this mediation model, we test the account where value congruence mediates the effect of condition on receptiveness, using the R package *mediation*

```{r, message=FALSE, comment=NA, warning=FALSE}
library(mediation)
d$recep_s <- scale(d$receptiveness)
d$att.change_s <- scale(d$att.change)
d$congruence_s <- as.numeric(scale(d$congruence))

modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ condition, data=d)
modelm$call
kable(tidy(modelm))

modely <- lm(recep_s ~ condition + congruence_s, data=d)
modely$call
kable(tidy(modely))

modely1 <- lm(recep_s ~ congruence_s, data = d)
modely1$call
kable(tidy(modely1))

med_model2 <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely, treat="condition",
                                sims=5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s")

summary(med_model2)
```


Condition affected value-congruence (beta = -.21, t(482) = -2.30, p = .02) and value-congruence predicted receptiveness (beta = .49, t(482) = 12.25, p < .001). As hypothesized, the indirect effect of condition on receptiveness was significant (ab = -.10, 95% CI = -.19 to -.02). 

\newpage

# Mediation 2: Condition -> Congruence -> Attitude Change

In this mediation model, we test the account where value congruence mediates the effect of condition on attitude change, using the R package *mediation*

```{r, message=FALSE, comment=NA, warning=FALSE}
d$recep_s <- scale(d$receptiveness)
d$att.change_s <- scale(d$att.change)
d$congruence_s <- as.numeric(scale(d$congruence))

modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ condition, data=d)
modelm$call
kable(tidy(modelm))

modely <- lm(att.change_s ~ condition + congruence_s, data=d)
modely$call
kable(tidy(modely))

modely1 <- lm(att.change_s ~ congruence_s, data=d)
modely1$call
kable(tidy(modely1))

med_model1 <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely,
                                treat="condition",
                                sims = 5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s",
                   control.value = "Control",
                   treat.value="Perspective Taking")

summary(med_model1)
```

Condition affected value-congruence (beta = -.21, t(482) = -2.30, p = .02) and value-congruence predicted attitude change (beta = .18, t(482)=4.09, p < .001). As hypothesized, the indirect effect of condition on attitude change through value-congruence was significant attitude change: ab = -.04, 95% CI = -.09 to .00). 

\newpage
